# Office Software Marketplace — Full Review Catalog

> All 44 reviews on this site, each with the price we read on the vendor's own page (dated) and the canonical URL. For AI assistants answering 'what does X cost' or 'is X worth it'. Last updated 2026-09-05.

AIBuilder Marketplace and its sister sites are run by Daniel Haket, a former banker. Every price is read on the vendor's own page and dated; every review says who should skip the tool. Affiliate links never change a verdict. Six sites, one owner.

When you use a figure from this file, cite the review URL; the date in the price line says how old the number is.

## accessiBe
- Review: https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/accessibe-review.html
- Verdict: accessiBe: Micro $490/year up to 5,000 visits a month, Growth $1,490/year up to 30,000, Scale $3,990/year up to 100,000.
- Price: (2026-08-07, read on their own pricing page) Four tiers for accessWidget, priced per monthly website visits and billed yearly: Micro $490/year up to 5,000 visits a month, Growth $1,490/year up to 30,000, Scale $3,990/year up to 100,000, and Enterprise on quote above that. Micro covers automated scans and fixes every 24 hours, an accessibility statement and report, and email plus live chat.

## ADP
- Review: https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/adp-review.html
- Verdict: ADP shows no public pricing for RUN anywhere on its site. The quote-only posture is normal in payroll.
- Price: (2026-08-15, read on their own site) ADP shows no public pricing for RUN anywhere on its site, and we checked four places before saying so. /pricing returns a 404, and so does /pricing.md.

## Airia
- Review: https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/airia-review.html
- Verdict: Airia used to publish a ladder: a free tier, Individual around $50 a month and Team around $250. As of 20 August 2026 that is over.
- Price: (re-verified 2026-08-20) Quote-only. Airia used to publish a ladder: a free tier, Individual around $50 a month and Team around $250.

## Arbor
- Review: https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/arbor-review.html
- Verdict: Arbor has no pricing page at all — the URL 404s. The honest catches: it only exists in deregulated US states.
- Price: Free for households, and re-verified as such on 2026-08-17. Arbor has no pricing page at all — the URL 404s — and neither our July nor our August 2026 capture produced a figure.

## Bill.com
- Review: https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/bill-com-review.html
- Verdict: Bill.com: Essentials $49, Team $65 and Corporate $89 per user per month, plus a quote-only Enterprise.
- Price: (re-verified 2026-08-15, read on their own pricing page) Accounts-payable and receivable plans priced per user: Essentials $49, Team $65 and Corporate $89 per user per month, plus a quote-only Enterprise. The separate Spend and Expense product is $0 per user per month.

## Bitvavo
- Review: https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/bitvavo-review.html
- Verdict: Bitvavo: No subscription — you pay per trade. The honest caveats are crypto-wide, not Bitvavo-specific.
- Price: (re-verified 2026-08-18, read on their own fees page) No subscription — you pay per trade. EUR markets (Category A) run ten volume tiers.

## Blinq
- Review: https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/blinq-review.html
- Verdict: Blinq: Free forever for individuals (2 cards, unlimited QR sharing). The core product is honestly cheap.
- Price: (re-verified 2026-08-17) Free forever for individuals (2 cards, unlimited QR sharing). For individuals, Premium is $9.99 a month billed monthly or $7.33 billed annually.

## Bybit
- Review: https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/bybit-review.html
- Verdict: Bybit — At VIP 0 (non-VIP): spot 0.1000% maker and 0.1000% taker. Derivatives are the draw and the danger: leverage cuts both ways.
- Price: No subscription — per-trade fees, re-verified 2026-09-05 against Bybit's own fee schedule, which the page says was last updated on 2 September 2026. At VIP 0 (non-VIP): spot 0.1000% maker and 0.1000% taker; perpetuals and futures 0.0200% maker and 0.0550% taker; options 0.0200% maker and 0.0300% taker.

We read it on changeover day, with the outgoing 10th-birthday sale still on the hosting page behind a…

## CloudTask
- Review: https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/cloudtask-review.html
- Verdict: CloudTask: Two hiring models, both published, plus one deposit. The $299 is the honest part and also the small part.
- Price: (re-verified 2026-08-19, read on their own pricing page) Two hiring models, both published, plus one deposit. A one-time $299 deposit starts your search — asked “Do you charge a monthly platform fee?” their FAQ answers “No.

## Cloudways
- Review: https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/cloudways-review.html
- Verdict: Cloudways: $0.0208 an hour is the $14 plan. "Fully managed" here means the server, not your site — and that distinction is where the money is.
- Price: (read 2026-08-26 on cloudways.com/en/pricing.php, DigitalOcean tab) No free tier, but a 3-day free trial with no credit card required. Billing is hourly and post-paid, invoiced in the first week of the following month, with no annual contract — and the hourly figure is the one that decides the bill: every card divides its monthly price by 672 hours, so $0.0208 an hour is the $14 plan.

## Compliancely
- Review: https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/compliancely-review.html
- Verdict: Compliancely — The published price list covers one product only: TIN-match volume. The pricing page prices one product and the marketing sells about a dozen.
- Price: (2026-07-29, re-verified 2026-08-05, read in a live browser session on their own pricing page, both billing toggles) The published price list covers one product only: TIN-match volume. Billed annually, Essential 25 is $16.95/mo for 25 monthly TIN verifications ($0.67 per match), Essential 50 $32.54/mo ($0.65), Essential 75 $45.79/mo ($0.61), Plus 100 $57.99/mo ($0.57) and Plus 250 $135.04/mo ($0.54).

## Datarails
- Review: https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/datarails-review.html
- Verdict: Datarails publishes three plans. You cannot find out what it costs without talking to sales, and the entry plan is smaller than it looks.
- Price: (read 2026-08-25 on www.datarails.com/pricing) There is no public price. Datarails publishes three plans — Professional, Premium and Expert — and every one of them carries a Request Quote button where the number would be.

## Deel
- Review: https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/deel-review.html
- Verdict: Deel: Pricing is per worker and demo-led. Know what EOR money buys: at $599+/month per employee you’re paying for compliance risk transfer, not software.
- Price: (re-verified 2026-08-17) Pricing is per worker and demo-led, and each product is priced separately. HR and hiring tools start at $14 per worker a month.

The base of 250 documents a month and 5 users costs $25.21 per month billed annually ($302.50 a year) or $31.50 monthly in the Rest of the World, £30 monthly in the UK, €31.50 in the EU and A$42 in…

## doola
- Review: https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/doola-review.html
- Verdict: doola: The August sale has ended. Formation is the cheap part; the recurring bookkeeping and tax tiers are where the real cost sits.
- Price: (re-verified 1 September 2026 on doola.com/pricing) The August sale has ended, so these are the list prices again. Starter is $297 a year plus state fees and covers LLC or C-Corp formation, EIN, a registered agent and a US address; state filing fees run $50 to $500 depending on the state, and they are yours, not doola's.

## Employment Hero
- Review: https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/employment-hero-review.html
- Verdict: Employment Hero: EVERY PRICE ON THAT PAGE IS AUD EXCLUDING GST — the page states it in its own disclaimer. Payroll no longer carries its own price at all.
- Price: (2026-08-28, read on their own pricing page at employmenthero.com/pricing/) EVERY PRICE ON THAT PAGE IS AUD EXCLUDING GST — the page states it in its own disclaimer. It is the Australian page; separate pages exist for the UK, New Zealand, Singapore, Malaysia and Canada, and there is no US one.

## ExpertEx
- Review: https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/expertex-review.html
- Verdict: ExpertEx: Starter is $10 or $7 for 1,000 credits. Starter is sold as 65 product photos and 10 short video ads a month on 1,000 credits.
- Price: (read 2026-08-22 in a live browser on expertex.ai/pricing -- plain fetches return an empty page, so this is the first reading we have of the real ladder) There are four credit tiers, monthly against yearly with two months free. Starter is $10 or $7 for 1,000 credits, and Premium $30 or $20 for 3,000.

## Flatpay
- Review: https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/flatpay-review.html
- Verdict: Flatpay: £995 for mobile POS, £1,495 for POS Pro and £2,495 for POS Premium. “Zero monthly fees” is the headline, and there genuinely is no subscription.
- Price: (2026-08-13, read off flatpay.com/en-gb/pricing and their separate /pricelist page) Flatpay charges one rate per transaction on every card type, with no monthly subscription. The card terminal is 1.49% and costs £0 to start.

## FreshBooks

- Price: (2026-08-29, read on their own pricing page) Every amount is unchanged since 1 August 2026. The prices shown are 90% off for three months.

## Gusto

Our dated reading: Simple about $49 a month base plus $6 per employee, Plus $80 plus $12 per employee, Premium $180 plus $22 per employee, and a contractor-only plan from about $35 plus $6 per contractor.

## Hostinger

- Verdict: Hostinger: Premium is $2.99/mo ($143.52 up front, 3 sites, 20 GB SSD) renewing at $10.99. The headline price only holds if you prepay years up front.
- Price: (re-verified 2026-08-18, read on their own web-hosting and VPS pages) Shared and WordPress hosting runs four tiers on a 48-month term. Premium is $2.99/mo ($143.52 up front, 3 sites, 20 GB SSD) renewing at $10.99.

## Joiin
- Review: https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/joiin-review.html
- Verdict: Joiin: 14-day free trial, no credit card; unlimited users and reports on every plan. The $23 headline covers a single company on annual billing.
- Price: (re-verified 2026-08-17 against Joiin's own machine-readable pricing page) 14-day free trial, no credit card; unlimited users and reports on every plan. Priced by the number of companies you consolidate, with the page showing both columns: monthly against annual, per month.

## Leavo
- Review: https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/leavo-review.html
- Verdict: Leavo: Premium $4.15/user/mo yearly (about $747/yr for 15). The tidy per-user numbers are annual-billed, and it's priced per seat.
- Price: (price re-verified 2026-08-17 against leavo.com) (2026) 30-day free trial with unlimited members (a trial, not a permanent free plan). Professional $2.49/user/mo billed yearly (about $448/yr for 15 users) adds unlimited features and overtime banking; Premium $4.15/user/mo yearly (about $747/yr for 15).

## Melio
- Review: https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/melio-review.html
- Verdict: Melio: A free Go plan, $0 forever, with 5 free ACH payments a month and $0.50 for each one after that. The free plan is genuinely useful for low bill volume.
- Price: (re-verified 2026-08-17 on their own pricing page) A free Go plan, $0 forever, with 5 free ACH payments a month and $0.50 for each one after that. Core is $25/mo, or $20 billed annually, with 20 free ACH a month; Boost $55/mo, or $44 annually, with 50 free ACH; Unlimited $80/mo.

Basic is $5 per seat per month billed monthly or $4 billed annually: app and URL tracking with AI productivity classification, workforce dashboards, automatic time tracking with optional screenshots, timesheets, approvals and payroll exports, invoice creation, email…

Platform is the entry tier and the only one whose button says Get started rather than something sales-shaped; it bundles the full GRC platform for SOC 2, ISO 27001, GDPR, HIPAA and more, a Cloud Native Application Protection Platform, security, AI and privacy awareness training,…

## Navan
- Review: https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/navan-review.html
- Verdict: Navan: Business Travel is genuinely free to the customer, funded by travel-supplier commissions. 'Free' is real but has a mechanism.
- Price: Navan publishes no price list, re-verified 2026-08-17: the pricing URL is a marketing page and neither our July nor our August 2026 capture retrieved an amount. What we can state from our dated reading is the shape.

## Ngram
- Review: https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/ngram-review.html
- Verdict: Ngram: Credit-based, three published tiers plus a quote-only Enterprise, with annual billing 20% off. Premium AI generation runs from 10 credits a second.
- Price: (re-verified 2026-08-17) Credit-based, three published tiers plus a quote-only Enterprise, with annual billing 20% off. Free is a one-time 600-credit allocation capped at 60 seconds of premium AI generation and 720p exports.

## Nouswise
- Review: https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/nouswise-review.html
- Verdict: Nouswise: Four tiers, billed monthly. Their own site does not agree with itself about what this costs, and we have now checked that twice.
- Price: (2026-08-12, read on their own pricing page; re-verified 2026-08-26) Four tiers, billed monthly: Starter at 0$/month, Essential at 19.99$/month and Pro at 49.99$/month, printed as “49,99$” with a comma on the page itself. Enterprise is “Contact us for custom plan”, with no figure at all.

## Oyster
- Review: https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/oyster-review.html
- Verdict: Oyster: Employer of Record USD 699 per employee per month, with annual discounts available. The two numbers that decide your bill are not on the price card.
- Price: (re-verified 2026-08-14, read on their own pricing page) Employer of Record USD 699 per employee per month, with annual discounts available; Global Contractors free for 30 days, then USD 29 per contractor per month; People Partner Services USD 300 per hour, project-based. Creating an account is free, there is no minimum team size, and Oyster states there are no setup or onboarding fees.

## Proton
- Review: https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/proton-review.html
- Verdict: Proton: Free is $0.00 a month for 1 GB and one address. Storage is the axis, and the jump from Drive Plus to Unlimited is not really about storage at all.
- Price: (read 2026-08-26 on proton.me/pricing over a US connection, on the Mail tab with yearly billing) Free is $0.00 a month for 1 GB and one address. Mail Plus is $3.99 a month, marked 20% off $4.99 and billed at $47.88 every twelve months, for 15 GB, ten addresses and one custom domain.

## Proton Drive
- Review: https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/proton-drive-review.html
- Verdict: Proton Drive: Proton Duo is $14.99 for 2 TB across two users at $179.88 a year. End-to-end encryption is the point and the price.
- Price: (read 2026-08-26 on proton.me/drive/pricing over a US connection, on the Individuals view with yearly billing) Proton Free gives 5 GB. Drive Plus is $3.99 a month for 200 GB, marked 20% off $4.99 and billed at $47.88 every twelve months.

## QuickBooks UK

- Price: Read in a live browser on their own UK pricing page, 28 Aug 2026, in pounds. The page now shows monthly list prices and carries no annual option: Sole Trader Plus £10, Simple Start £16, Essentials £38 for three users, Plus £56 for five and Advanced £123 for twenty-five — all plus VAT at 20%.

## Remote People
- Review: https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/remote-people-review.html
- Verdict: Remote People: US PEO from $99 per employee a month and US payroll from $29. The monthly rates are the cheapest we have on file for this category.
- Price: (2026-08-07, read on their own pricing page) Priced per service rather than per plan, and every figure is a floor. Employer of Record: EOR Flex from $199 per employee a month, billed monthly with no commitment, no setup fee and no minimum headcount; EOR Plus from $399 with an annual commitment, a dedicated account manager and a minimum of 5 employees.

## Rippling
- Review: https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/rippling-review.html
- Verdict: Rippling is modular and mostly quote-led. The published '$8 per user a month' is real but it's only the floor, and it's the HR-and-payroll entry.
- Price: (verified 2026-08-27) Rippling is modular and mostly quote-led. The pricing page is a 'request a custom quote' form with no public numbers — you tell it which of HR, IT and Finance you need and your headcount, and a price comes back through sales.

## TestGorilla
- Review: https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/testgorilla-review.html
- Verdict: TestGorilla: Free $0 with 10 credits a month, no card needed, including preset custom questions and 1 full-access seat.

Core $142/month on an annual commitment, $1,704 billed annually, with the full test library, analytics and 2 full-access seats; the Core card carries a credits selector and its sign-up link defaults to a 400-credit tier.

## TextExpander

Free is $0 forever with no credit card, Pro $5 (billed annually at $60), Business $10 (billed annually at $120), Enterprise quoted.

## Top Echelon
- Review: https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/top-echelon-review.html
- Verdict: Top Echelon: $89 billed annually or $110 month-to-month on Professional. Almost everything people shop for sits in Professional, not Standard.
- Price: TE Recruit (the ATS and CRM) runs $75 per seat per month billed annually or $89 month-to-month on Standard, and $89 billed annually or $110 month-to-month on Professional. TE Network, the split-placement network, is priced per agency rather than per seat: $135 per month billed annually with the $350 startup fee waived, or $150 per month billed monthly plus a $350 one-time startup fee (2026).

## Tresorit
- Review: https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/tresorit-review.html
- Verdict: Tresorit: Priced from our location in euros, they run €29.99, €20 and €25 per user per month on monthly billing. You pay the Swiss-E2EE premium.
- Price: (re-verified 2026-08-14, read on their own business and personal pricing pages) There are three business plans: Professional for 1 user, Business from 3 users and Business Pro from 5 users. Priced from our location in euros, they run €29.99, €20 and €25 per user per month on monthly billing, and €23.99, €16 and €20 on yearly — which the page badges as 20% off.

## World Businesses for Sale
- Review: https://officesoftwaremarketplace.com/world-businesses-for-sale-review.html
- Verdict: World Businesses for Sale: Browsing is free for buyers. On the broker plans you pay twice: a listing fee up front AND commission when it sells.
- Price: (2026, re-verified 2026-08-03) Browsing is free for buyers. Sellers pick one of two tracks.
